title: He was executed at 19 for plotting an armed uprising against British rule. Bhagat Singh later carried his photo.

sources.text: Scroll.in - The 1915 Ghadar plan to free India from the British was a failure - but it sparked a revolution

caption:
He was executed at 19 for plotting an armed uprising against British rule. Bhagat Singh later carried his photo.

A Ghadar Party revolutionary, Sarabha was arrested in March 1915 and convicted in the First Lahore Conspiracy Case for plotting an armed uprising against British colonial rule in Punjab.

Bhagat Singh, then a teenager, is said to have carried Sarabha's photograph and considered him a personal hero, carrying his example forward into the next generation of India's independence movement.

Sarabha didn't live to see independence - but the movement he died for outlived him by over three decades, carried forward by the people he inspired.
